title: VOID PVP — window.void bridge surface
description: The single `window.void` object that joins the Java mod and the in-game React app, as specified in PVP_ARCHITECTURE.md §6.5. Java to JS is push, delivered through `void.on(event, handler)` and batched once per frame; JS to Java is a direct call. The bridge is in-process (Ultralight lives inside the JVM, §6.2), so calls are synchronous and return real applied state -- there is no ack, no optimistic UI and no request id. This file therefore does not describe a transport; it describes, per event, the shape of the payload handed to the handler, and per call, the positional `params` and the `returns` value. An instance of this schema is one enveloped event, call or call result, which is exactly the form the browser `?debug` harness of §9 records and replays against a fake window.void. Payloads are additionalProperties:false: unlike protocol.json this surface is not forward-compatible across versions, because the mod JAR embeds the UI bundle and the two always ship as one binary.

oneOf.description: A Java to JS event push.
The value a JS to Java call returned.

event_name.title: Event name
event_name.description: The seven channels Java pushes on. Closed set; `void.on` with any other name is a programming error.

call_name.title: Call name
call_name.description: The six methods JS may call on `window.void`. Closed set.

event.title: Event
event.description: One push from Java to JS, enveloped as {e, payload}. In the real bridge the envelope does not exist on the wire: `payload` is the single argument the `void.on(e, handler)` handler receives.

oneOf.description: The loadout library changed, or was delivered for the first time.
One mod setting changed outside the UI's own call.

payload.description: The whole library, in library order.
The mod, the key and the value Java stored.
Whether the menu is now open.

keys_payload.title: keys payload
keys_payload.description: Edge-triggered key state, pushed only when a key changes, from `KeyBinding.setKeyBindState` (§6.6). Each field is 0 for released and 1 for pressed -- integers, not booleans, so the UI can index a sprite row and so that a future analogue axis fits without a shape change. In HUD mode Ultralight receives no input events at all (§6.3); this event is how the player's keys reach the UI, as data. The renderer must touch only the changed key's node (§9).

lmb.description: Left mouse button state. The CPS mod derives clicks per second from the rising edges of this field (§3).

tick_payload.title: tick payload
tick_payload.description: All per-tick telemetry, coalesced into one push per game tick, i.e. 20 Hz (§6.6). Every HUD mod other than keystrokes and CPS reads from this. Fields whose sensor has nothing to report are omitted rather than sent as null, so a handler must treat an absent field as unchanged.

ping.description: Round-trip time in milliseconds from the player's own `NetworkPlayerInfo.responseTime`; -1 when unknown, such as in singleplayer or before the player list arrives.

armor.description: Worn armor and, when enabled, the held item. Present only on the ticks where durability or the equipped set changed.

fx.description: Active potion effects. Present only on the ticks where the effect set changed.

position.title: Position
position.description: Player position and yaw from `EntityPlayerSP`, read once per tick. Pitch is deliberately absent: no mod in §3 uses it.

y.description: World Y in blocks, feet level.

yaw.description: Facing in degrees, normalised to [-180, 180). The coordinates mod derives the cardinal direction from this.

armor_slot.title: Armor slot
armor_slot.description: One equipment slot from `InventoryPlayer.armorInventory`, or the held item when the armor status mod has `show_held_item` on.

item.description: Minecraft item id such as `diamond_chestplate`, or null when the slot is empty.

damage.description: Damage taken by the item. 0 is undamaged.

max_damage.description: Maximum durability of the item; 0 for items that do not take damage.

count.description: Stack size, relevant only for the held slot.

enchanted.description: Whether the item has any enchantment, so the UI can draw the glint treatment.

id.description: Numeric potion id as used by 1.8.9.

name.description: Unlocalised effect name such as `potion.moveSpeed`, for the UI to map to a label and icon.

amplifier.description: Amplifier level, 0-based: 0 renders as I, 1 as II.

duration_ms.description: Remaining duration in milliseconds, converted from ticks by the sensor so the UI never needs to know the tick rate.

ambient.description: Whether the effect comes from an ambient source such as a beacon; hidden when `hide_ambient` is set.

server_payload.title: server payload
server_payload.description: Pushed on connect and disconnect (§6.6). The same information also goes to Rust as the `server` protocol message.

host.description: Hostname of the server without port; empty string on disconnect.

connected.description: True on connect, false on disconnect.

loadout_payload.title: loadout payload
loadout_payload.description: The full active loadout. Pushed once on `hello` and again on every switch, whether the switch came from Rust, from the tray, from the L key or from `void.switchLoadout` (§6.5). The UI store treats this as a whole-state replacement.

loadouts_payload.title: loadouts payload
loadouts_payload.description: Every loadout in the library, in full and in library order, including the active one — exactly what Rust sent in `init.loadouts`. Pushed once on `init` and again whenever the library changes, so the in-game Loadouts frame (Figma 244:1130) can list and compare loadouts, and the quick palette can offer `Turn on in <other> loadout`, without a bridge accessor and without waiting to observe a `loadout` event per entry. Whole-state replacement, like `loadout`.

setting_payload.title: setting payload
setting_payload.description: One mod setting Java changed on its own — an in-game hotkey toggling a mod (the `keystrokes.keybind` overlay key), or a launcher-side `state` echo. It is *not* pushed for a change the page itself made through `setModSetting`: that call already returned the stored value, and re-pushing it would fight the control the player is holding. The UI applies it exactly as it applies the return value of `setModSetting`, so a whole-loadout replacement is not needed for a one-key change.

id.description: Which mod changed. Any of the 12.

key.description: Name of the setting, a property of that mod's settings sub-schema. `on` included.

value.description: The value Java stored, after clamping — the same value `setModSetting` would have returned.

menu_payload.title: menu payload
menu_payload.description: True when VoidMenuScreen opened, false when it closed. The React app draws the HUD layer and the menu layer into the same Ultralight view (§6.2); this flag is how it decides which is visible.

call.title: Call
call.description: One JS to Java call, enveloped as {c, params}. In the real bridge `params` is the positional argument list of the method.

oneOf.description: Move or scale a HUD item.
Change one setting of one mod.

call_result.title: Call result
call_result.description: The value one JS to Java call returned, enveloped as {c, returns}. Every call except `openKeybindCapture` returns synchronously, because the bridge is in-process (§6.5).

call_setGameplay.title: setGameplay call
call_setGameplay.description: `void.setGameplay(id, on)`. Writes the boolean field the mod's actuator Mixin reads every frame (§6.7). Synchronous and authoritative: the toggle in the UI shows the returned value, never an optimistic one.

items.description: Which gameplay mod to toggle. Only the five `kind: gameplay` mods are accepted; a HUD mod is a programming error.

setGameplay_returns.title: setGameplay returns
setGameplay_returns.description: The state actually applied. Normally equals the requested value; differs only if the mod refused the change.

result_setGameplay.title: setGameplay result
result_setGameplay.description: Envelope for a setGameplay return value.

call_setHud.title: setHud call
call_setHud.description: `void.setHud(id, placement)`. Called by the HUD editor on drop (§9). Java applies it to the live layout and mirrors the whole layout to Rust as the `hud` protocol message, which is what persists it.

items.description: The new placement. Same shape as a `hud_item` minus its `id`, which is the first argument.

anchor.description: Screen anchor the offsets are measured from.

dx.description: Horizontal offset in unscaled GUI pixels from the anchor.

dy.description: Vertical offset in unscaled GUI pixels from the anchor.

scale.description: Per-item size multiplier; omitted means leave unchanged.

setHud_returns.title: setHud returns
setHud_returns.description: The stored HUD item after snapping and clamping, so the editor can settle the dragged element on the value Java actually kept.

result_setHud.title: setHud result
result_setHud.description: Envelope for a setHud return value.

call_setModSetting.title: setModSetting call
call_setModSetting.description: `void.setModSetting(id, key, value)`. The generic writer behind every control in a mod's settings pane. The value must satisfy that mod's settings sub-schema in mods.json; Java clamps rather than throws when it does not.

items.description: Which mod to configure. Any of the 12.
Name of the setting, a property of that mod's settings sub-schema, e.g. `opacity`. `on` is settable here too, though gameplay mods should use `setGameplay`.
New value for the setting. Scalars only; no mod has an object- or array-valued setting.

setModSetting_returns.title: setModSetting returns
setModSetting_returns.description: The value actually stored, after clamping to the setting's range or enum. The control binds to this, not to what it sent.

result_setModSetting.title: setModSetting result
result_setModSetting.description: Envelope for a setModSetting return value.

call_switchLoadout.title: switchLoadout call
call_switchLoadout.description: `void.switchLoadout(id)`. Writes every actuator field and re-renders the HUD in under a frame (§8.2), then reports `state` to Rust. A `loadout` event follows with the new loadout, so the caller does not need the returned object.

items.description: Id of a loadout present in the library Java received in `init.loadouts`.

switchLoadout_returns.title: switchLoadout returns
switchLoadout_returns.description: True when a loadout with that id existed and was applied; false when it did not, in which case nothing changed.

result_switchLoadout.title: switchLoadout result
result_switchLoadout.description: Envelope for a switchLoadout return value.

call_closeMenu.title: closeMenu call
call_closeMenu.description: `void.closeMenu()`. Closes VoidMenuScreen and returns the mouse to the game, the same thing the menu key does. A `menu` event with payload false follows.

closeMenu_returns.title: closeMenu returns
closeMenu_returns.description: Always null; the call has no result.

result_closeMenu.title: closeMenu result
result_closeMenu.description: Envelope for a closeMenu return value.

call_openKeybindCapture.title: openKeybindCapture call
call_openKeybindCapture.description: `void.openKeybindCapture(modId)`. The one asynchronous call on the bridge. It is still one synchronous hop like every other call, but the hop only **arms** the capture: Java answers `{c: 'openKeybindCapture', returns: null}` immediately, meaning "armed", and keeps key input until the player presses something. The key itself arrives later on the push channel, as a *call-result* envelope delivered through `__emit`: `__emit({c: 'openKeybindCapture', returns: 'V'})`, or `returns: null` when the player cancelled with Escape. The shim turns the armed answer into a pending Promise and the later envelope into its resolution, in FIFO order; the Promise never rejects. Because a null arrives on both channels, a shim must never read the synchronous null as the resolution — that is the one way to get this wrong. The captured key is not stored by this call; the UI writes it with `setModSetting(modId, 'key', captured)`.

items.description: The mod whose keybind is being captured, used only to label the capture prompt.

openKeybindCapture_returns.title: openKeybindCapture returns
openKeybindCapture_returns.description: Two different things travel in this shape, which is why it admits null twice over. The **synchronous** answer of `__void_native` is always null and means "capture armed". The **deferred** envelope, delivered later through `__emit`, carries the captured key — or null again when the player cancelled with Escape. A shim distinguishes them by channel, never by value: the synchronous answer opens a Promise, the `__emit` envelope resolves it.

oneOf.description: The captured key, delivered later through `__emit`.
Capture armed (the synchronous answer), or cancelled with Escape (the deferred one).

result_openKeybindCapture.title: openKeybindCapture result
result_openKeybindCapture.description: Envelope for an openKeybindCapture answer. Both the synchronous armed answer and the deferred resolution use it; only the channel tells them apart.

returns.description: Null when armed or cancelled; the captured key otherwise.
